standard_prerequisites.name: Localizing ring maps and the correspondence between localizations of a Noetherian ring and affine open subschemes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stacks Project, Algebra and Schemes (localization and affine opens)
standard_prerequisites.use: Background for replacing S and X by affine neighbourhoods and for the A_{ff'} -> B_{fg} localization argument.

core_obligations: Trim S by removing the finitely many irreducible components not containing s, then replace S and X by affine open neighbourhoods of s and x, so S = Spec(A), X = Spec(B) with primes p, q below s, x (proof lines 8927-8931).
Show A embeds into A_p: A is reduced and all minimal primes of A are contained in p (proof lines 8932-8933).

Use finite type to pick generators b_i of B over A, use A_p = B_q to find f notin p and a_i with b_i and a_i/f equal in B_q, and localize further at g to make A_f -> B_{fg} contain the images of all b_i and of g (proof lines 8934-8942).

Choose f' with f'/f^n representing the image of g in B_{fg}; conclude A_{ff'} -> B_{fg} is surjective, and injective because A_{ff'} lands inside A_p = B_q, hence an isomorphism (proof lines 8943-8948).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to affine schemes after dropping irrelevant irreducible components.
Obtain A subset A_p from reducedness and minimal primes inside p.
Approximate the generators of B by fractions from A_p = B_q and localize to make the ring map dominant and then surjective.
Use the embedding of A_{ff'} in A_p to get injectivity and conclude an isomorphism, i.e. an open immersion.
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that O_{X,x} = O_{S,s} for a finite-type morphism X -> S with S reduced with finitely many irreducible components forces an open neighbourhood of x on which f is an open immersion. The proof is a purely affine-local argument: trim S to its components through s, then write S = Spec(A), X = Spec(B); reducedness and containment of all minimal primes of A in p give A subset A_p, finite type gives generators b_i over A, and the equality A_p = B_q lets each b_i be approximated by a_i/f and then by f' so that A_{ff'} -> B_{fg} is first surjective and then injective, hence an isomorphism (proof lines 8927-8948). H2: the two-step localization to force both surjectivity and injectivity is the non-routine core.
